title: Grammar: Advanced Formal Discourse Markers and Analytical Connectors
grammarTip:
Продвинутые дискурсивные маркеры для академического письма:

ДОБАВЛЕНИЕ (более сильное чем "also"):
Furthermore · Moreover · In addition · What is more · Besides

КОНТРАСТ (более сильное чем "but"):
Nevertheless · Nonetheless · However · On the contrary · Conversely

ПОДТВЕРЖДЕНИЕ:
Indeed · In fact · As a matter of fact · Evidently · Clearly

ЦЕЛЬ / РЕЗУЛЬТАТ:
Consequently · Therefore · Thus · Hence · As a consequence

УСЛОВИЕ:
Provided that · On condition that · Assuming that · In the event that

💡 Используй маркеры точно по значению:
"Moreover" = добавляет более важное, чем предыдущее
"Conversely" = полная противоположность
"Hence" = поэтому (формальнее чем "so")

grammarTable.subject: to the extent that
grammarTable.short: in so far as / as much as
grammarTable.example: "This is problematic to the extent that it ignores the role of context in communication."

grammarTable.subject: insofar as / in so far as
grammarTable.example: "The model is useful insofar as it captures the key dimensions of cultural variation."

grammarTable.subject: in view of
grammarTable.example: "In view of the evidence, the native speaker model requires substantial revision."

grammarTable.subject: by virtue of
grammarTable.example: "By virtue of their multilingual background, these speakers have a communicative advantage."

grammarTable.subject: with a view to
grammarTable.short: with the aim of / in order to
grammarTable.example: "With a view to improving intercultural communication, the curriculum was redesigned."

grammarTable.subject: in the interests of
grammarTable.short: for the benefit of / to serve
grammarTable.example: "In the interests of equity, all language varieties should be treated with equal respect."

grammarExtra.title: To the Extent That / Insofar As: Degree and Qualification

rows.form: "to the extent that" = in so far as / to the degree that (qualifies a claim)
rows.example: "The policy is successful to the extent that it improves intelligibility without suppressing linguistic diversity."

rows.form: "insofar as / in so far as" = to the degree that (more formal, philosophical)
rows.example: "The distinction is useful insofar as it captures real differences in communicative style."

rows.form: Both introduce a qualifying clause that limits the scope of a claim
rows.example: "The model works… to the extent that conditions are met / insofar as the assumptions hold"

rows.form: Equivalent to "but only to the degree that" — adding precision
rows.example: "Correction is appropriate, to the extent that the error impedes understanding."

grammarExtra.title: In View Of / In Light Of: Reasoning from Evidence

rows.form: "In view of" = considering, given (formal)
rows.example: "In view of the evidence for cognitive benefits, multilingualism should be promoted in schools."

rows.form: "In light of" = taking into account, in the knowledge of
rows.example: "In light of recent research, the native speaker model requires revision."

rows.form: Both introduce a reason for a conclusion or proposal
rows.example: "In view of / In light of the challenges involved, a phased approach is recommended."

rows.form: "In view of the above / In light of what has been said" = formal conclusion signal
rows.example: "In view of the above, it can be concluded that language policy has direct social consequences."

grammarExtra.title: By Virtue Of: Cause and Qualification

rows.form: "By virtue of" = because of / on account of / as a result of (formal)
rows.example: "By virtue of their multilingual experience, these speakers navigate cultural differences more effectively."

rows.form: Used for circumstances that confer an advantage, status, or capability
rows.example: "By virtue of its global reach, English has become the default language of international science."

rows.form: "By virtue of the fact that" = because of the fact that
rows.example: "By virtue of the fact that English is widely taught, it has advantages as a lingua franca."

rows.form: More formal than "because of" — preferred in legal and academic texts
rows.example: "The right exists by virtue of the treaty." (legal language)

grammarExtra.title: With a View To / For the Purposes Of: Expressing Purpose

rows.form: "With a view to + gerund" = with the aim of / in order to
rows.example: "With a view to promoting intercultural understanding, exchange programmes were established."

rows.form: "For the purposes of + noun/gerund" = for the reason of / in order to (formal)
rows.example: "For the purposes of this analysis, ELF is defined as English used between non-native speakers."

rows.form: Both are more formal than "in order to" or "to"
rows.example: "The curriculum was redesigned with a view to developing intercultural competence."

rows.form: "In the interests of + noun/gerund" = for the benefit of
rows.example: "In the interests of accuracy, it should be noted that the data refers only to written English."

grammarExtra.title: Common Errors with Advanced Formal Phrases

rows.form: ❌ To the extent of that the model is useful…
rows.example: ✅ To the extent that the model is useful… ("to the extent THAT" — never "to the extent of that")

rows.form: ❌ By virtue to their experience…
rows.example: ✅ By virtue of their experience… ("by virtue OF" — always "of")

rows.form: ❌ With a view to improve intercultural skills…
rows.example: ✅ With a view to improving intercultural skills… ("with a view to + gerund")

rows.form: ❌ In the interests to equity…
rows.example: ✅ In the interests of equity… ("in the interests OF" — always "of")

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses a formal discourse marker correctly?
opts: "In the interests to clarity, let me restate the argument."
"In the interests of clarity, let me restate the argument."
"By the interests of clarity, let me restate."
"For interests of clarity, let me restate."
exercises.correct: "In the interests of clarity, let me restate the argument."

exercises.hint: "By virtue of" = because of / on account of (formal)
